hypotheses.justification: hm follows from hmp together with the variable [Fact p.Prime], which is an argument of the theorem because p occurs in the statement. If m = 0, then Nat.Coprime 0 p says gcd 0 p = p = 1 (Nat.coprime_zero_left). That contradicts p being prime, since a prime is > 1. So 0 < m always holds under the remaining hypotheses, and the statement stays true after deleting hm. In the proof, hm is only used to build the witness ⟨m, hm, hpm, _⟩ for hinj and hsurj. Replace it by a local `have hm : 0 < m := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (fun h => by subst h; have := Nat.coprime_zero_left p |>.mp hmp; exact (Fact.out : p.Prime).one_lt.ne' this)`. The rest of the proof is unchanged.
